title: CertOps Trust Anchor Job Payload
description: Signed dispatch payload for a distribute-trust or revoke-trust job (ADR-0012 decisions 4 and 6). A trust anchor has no private key and no renewal, so this is a sibling contract file, not a discriminated branch on job-payload.schema.json: forcing a trust job through the certificate schema would mean either making certificateId/keyMode conditionally required (which makes every future certificate-job field ask whether it applies under the trust branch too) or relaxing job-payload.schema.json's required array, weakening validation for every existing certificate job. Composes the shared signed-dispatch-payload definition (schemaVersion/jobId/workspaceId/agentId/mode/requestedAt plus the signed-dispatch fields) and adds only what a trust operation needs: trustAnchorId, anchorType, fingerprintSha256, pem, requestedBy, metadata. additionalProperties: false at every level, so a trust job can never be mistaken for, or grown into, a certificate job. agentId is required here from day one because this schema is new, the same rationale protocol-smoke-payload.schema.json documents. The wire-only signature field is referenced from signed-dispatch-wire-v1.schema.json rather than defined here, because a signature is never part of the content it signs.

trustAnchorId.description: certops_trust_anchors.id (text-cast), the row this job distributes to or revokes from a machine trust store. Also the value stored in certificate_jobs.subject_id for a trust job (subject_type 'trust_anchor', ADR-0012 decision 5).

action.description: Agent-facing action mirrors the control-plane operation 1:1 (ADR-0012 decision 14): a trust job's control-plane intent and agent-side action are the same concept, with no multi-step lifecycle to distinguish the way issue/renew needed one.

anchorType.description: Required and part of the signed payload: the routing decision for WHICH machine trust store the anchor belongs in. A root belongs in LocalMachine\Root and an intermediate in LocalMachine\CA; this must not be inferred at execution time from the certificate's own basicConstraints/issuer fields, because the PEM is untrusted input and inference would make the destination store a property of the material rather than of the approved intent. The agent derives the concrete Windows store name from this value; a store name is never accepted as a payload field, which would be a second, disagreeable source of truth (ADR-0012 decision 4).

fingerprintSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the trust anchor PEM, carried on both the certops_trust_anchors row and every job payload referencing it, so the agent can verify the anchor it is about to install or remove against the fingerprint the control plane signed.

transitionGeneration.description: The certops_trust_anchor_installations.transition_generation this dispatch is fulfilling (ADR-0012 decision 20a/20c). Resolved at dispatch time from the installation row rather than stored on the job payload, because the stored payload is fingerprinted into creation_request_hash and must stay stable across idempotent replays. The agent echoes this value back on its result (trust-result-contract.schema.json requires it) and records it in its ownership receipt, which is what lets the server reject a superseded transition's late result as stale (decision 20f).

pem.description: Public CA certificate PEM to install. Required for distribute-trust and rejected for revoke-trust (see allOf below): revocation is identified by trustAnchorId plus fingerprintSha256 alone, which is all the agent needs to find and remove the anchor, and accepting a PEM there would invite a 'revoke this, but here is different material' ambiguity.
